title: Awarapan 2 Crosses Rs 113 Crore in First Week, Becomes Emraan Hashmi's Biggest Solo Hit
excerpt: The Vishesh Films sequel earned Rs 161 crore worldwide in seven days, dominating the Independence Day box office and leaving Sunny Deol's Batwara 1947 far behind.
body:
• Awarapan 2 earned Rs 113.50 crore nett in India in its opening week, becoming the highest-grossing solo Emraan Hashmi film and crossing Rs 161 crore worldwide.
  • The Vishesh Films sequel dominated the Independence Day box office clash, outpacing Sunny Deol's Batwara 1947 by a margin of nearly Rs 80 crore in domestic collections.
  • Day 7 brought in Rs 6 crore nett from over 10,800 screens, with a modest 11% decline from the previous day signaling strong weekday holds.
  • With no major competition until Toxic arrives, the film is positioned for a significant second-weekend spike and a potential blockbuster verdict.

First Week: Rs 113 Crore and Counting

Emraan Hashmi's romantic action drama Awarapan 2 has wrapped up its first week at the Indian box office with a nett collection of Rs 113.50 crore, according to tracking data from Sacnilk. The worldwide gross stands at Rs 161.67 crore, including Rs 26.30 crore from overseas markets and a domestic gross of Rs 135.37 crore.

The opening week makes Awarapan 2 the first solo Emraan Hashmi starrer to cross the Rs 100 crore nett mark domestically and the Rs 150 crore milestone globally, surpassing the lifetime collections of his previous hits including Raaz: The Mystery Continues.

Directed by Nitin Kakkar and produced under the Vishesh Films banner, the sequel co-stars Disha Patani and Shabana Azmi.

Day-by-Day Breakdown

Released on August 14 — India's Independence Day — Awarapan 2 capitalized on the extended holiday window. It opened to Rs 22 crore on Friday before surging 55% on Saturday to Rs 33.75 crore, helped by an increase in screenings from 9,033 to 10,496 shows. Sunday brought Rs 26 crore, rounding out a powerful opening weekend.

The weekday hold was solid. Monday delivered Rs 9.25 crore, while Tuesday held steady at Rs 9.75 crore with an uptick in screen count. Wednesday dipped 16% to Rs 6.75 crore, and Day 7 on Thursday came in at Rs 6 crore across 10,832 shows — a relatively gentle 11% drop.

The sustained weekday numbers above Rs 6 crore through the first week are a strong signal. For a Bollywood film with mixed critical reception, holding that floor suggests genuine audience pull rather than just holiday-driven front-loading.

Independence Day Box Office Clash: Awarapan 2 vs Batwara 1947

The Independence Day 2026 release window turned into a two-horse race, and Awarapan 2 won decisively. Rajkumar Santoshi's partition drama Batwara 1947, starring Sunny Deol, Preity Zinta, and Shabana Azmi, finished its first week at Rs 33.60 crore nett in India — less than a third of Awarapan 2's haul.

Batwara 1947's worldwide gross stands at Rs 47.62 crore, roughly Rs 2.4 crore short of the Rs 50 crore global mark as it heads into a second weekend facing steep competition for screens.

The gap is striking given that both films featured veteran stars and had significant production budgets. Awarapan 2's edge came from the cult following of the original 2007 film, whose music and emotional storyline turned it into a late-blooming fan favorite — a nostalgia factor the sequel successfully monetized.

What's Next: A Clear Run Toward Blockbuster

Awarapan 2 faces no significant new competition until Toxic arrives in cinemas, giving it a relatively clear runway for its second weekend. Industry trackers expect a spike in collections on Saturday and Sunday, which could push the film toward a blockbuster verdict.

With a reported 151% return on investment after just one week, the film has already turned a strong profit for Vishesh Films. A sustained second week above Rs 3-4 crore daily would put a Rs 140-150 crore nett lifetime within reach.

For Emraan Hashmi, the result marks a genuine career milestone. After a string of underwhelming theatrical runs, Awarapan 2 has re-established his box office viability — at least when paired with the right brand of familiar IP.
